knowledge_base.provenance: Illustrative classroom simulation rules proposed for software demonstration; not validated against a manufacturer manual, domain expert, or measured robot faults.

scenario.title: Warehouse Corridor Changes
scenario.description: Synthetic warehouse shelves frame a central aisle. Close one central cell, move along the replanned route, reopen the aisle, and continue.

events.label: Move one legal step on the replanned route

units.distance: Manhattan grid cells, capped at five for fuzzy input
units.speed: fractional grid moves per discrete simulation tick
units.battery: independent illustrative percentage input, not measured telemetry

fleet_simulation.stop_priority: diagnosis and zero battery > fuzzy proposal > traffic reservation

numerical_method.implication: clip each consequent membership at its rule activation
numerical_method.quadrature: composite trapezoidal quadrature over the uniform speed grid

sugeno.numerical_method: finite weighted sum; no output-universe sampling

provenance.singletons: analytic centroids of the corresponding speed triangles

limitations: This output is an illustrative speed recommendation, not a physical robot command.
The thresholds are not field-calibrated and membership degrees are not probabilities.
This controller does not implement stop safety, collision avoidance, or reservation checks.
The caller must override motion using diagnostics and reservations when required.
Mamdani centroid integration is approximated with composite trapezoidal quadrature on a 0.5 percent grid.
Mamdani and zero-order Sugeno can return different outputs because their inference and aggregation differ.
Illustrative memberships and rules are not calibrated to physical robots.
Battery percentages and categorical diagnostic observations are separate inputs.
One-tick reservations prevent the checked discrete conflicts, not all deadlocks.
A simulation tick has no conversion to physical time or braking distance.
